newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO STOCKS END HIGHER, BLUE-CHIPS UPBEAT.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO STOCKS END HIGHER, BLUE-CHIPS UPBEAT.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed higher on Wednesday, as shares of major multinational companies continued to attract investors, supported by the yen's retreat against the dollar. But the market's upside was capped by strong selling demand, brokers said.
The key Nikkei 225 average rose 228.79 points, or 1.26 percent, to end at 18,409.96. It had briefly climbed as high as 18,520.76. Its March futures were 190 points higher at 18,390.
"The yen eased sufficiently and this will benefit (blue-chip) firms' earnings," said Kazuo Shiogai, deputy branch manager at ING Baring Securities (Japan) Ltd.

Sentiment was brightened by a rally in export-oriented firms, such as Honda Motor Co Ltd and Toyota Motor Corp, which jumped to record highs, and Sony Corp , which surged to a new high for the financial year.

"These issues are supported by solid earnings growth and meet global investment standards, as they are based on group earnings," said an analyst at a second-tier Japanese securities house. Many firms in Japan still report parent-only earnings.
The market was also supported by gains in pharmaceutical firms, as their profits are not entirely tied to the country's sluggish economy, brokers said.
Banking issues were mixed on Wednesday.

Anxiety over the sector lingered in the market even though concerns had eased following Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's Monday comments that authorities would firmly support the top 20 Japanese banks in their efforts to resolve their bad loan problems, brokers said.

They said the sector's hopes were boosted by the possibility of public funds being used to help resolve banks' bad loan problems. The head of a major bankers body said the issue of using public money to protect depositors from banks' financial dificulties should be debated.
Turnover on the first section was 457 million shares on Wednesday, up from Monday's 340 million shares. The market was closed on Tuesday for a national holiday.
The broader-based TOPIX index gained 13.54 points, or one percent, to end at 1,368.43. The Nikkei 300 average closed up 3.38 points, or 1.31 percent, at 262.24.
Despite the gains in the indices, declining issues marginally outnumbered gainers 552 to 523, while 160 issues were unchanged.
Brokers said there was strong profit-taking demand at the upside ahead of the March 31 corporate book closings.

"The 18,500-level (in the Nikkei 225) has been tested many times today, but it could not be broken through. This is because fundamental factors (in the domestic economy) have not changed," one fund manager said.

By sector, gainers were led by miscellaneous manufacturing, retailers, services, automobiles, and railway/bus. The major losing sectors were gas, mining, electric power, sea transport and construction.
Honda ended up 130 yen at 3,510 yen in heavy trading, after briefly reaching 3,550 yen. Its previous all-time high was 3,520 yen, hit on November 27, 1996.
Toyota Motor Corp ended up 110 yen at 3,360. Its previous record high was 3,350 yen.
Sony Corp surged by 350 yen to 8,900 yen, above its previous high for this financial year of 8,560 yen.
In the currency market, the dollar rose above 124 yen in Tokyo trading against 122.80 yen in late Tokyo on Monday.

Some drug makers' shares jumped to new highs. Sankyo Co Ltd closed up 170 yen at 3,710 yen, far above its life-time high of 3,540 yen. Takeda Chemical Industries Co Ltd finished up 70 yen at 2,550 yen, above its previous high for the financial year of 2,490 yen.
